content:
After previewing at the I/O 2026 conference held in May, the macOS version of Gemini is now launching advanced voice control features.

Google positions this feature as allowing you to "speak naturally in any window on your desktop," and offers two main capabilities.

The first is a smart dictation feature that can "transcribe dictated content into clean, polished text." Gemini automatically removes filler words such as "um" and "ah," while recognising corrections made mid-sentence to accurately capture the key points you wish to express.

The formatted text will be entered at the location of your current cursor. This will provide a voice-to-text experience similar to what Gboard Rambler offers on the upcoming Gemini Intelligence phone.

The other feature goes beyond simple transcription, understanding the context of your current screen to execute complex tasks. This feature, which requires users to enable it manually, asks you to turn on Gemini reasoning in the app's settings.

  • Capture and summarise information: mark local files, images, or documents on your desktop, then tell Gemini directly what you need. For example, you could say: "Read these veterinary documents, and email a summary of my dog's medical records to the pet boarding centre."
  • Write and rewrite text: mark text anywhere on screen, then use voice to instantly rewrite, adjust the tone, and place the polished version exactly where you need it. Try saying: "Rewrite these notes into an executive summary, and add a TL;DR at the top."
  • Generate and edit images: use voice to create visual content, whether you're brainstorming concepts, enriching a travel itinerary, or making quick modifications to an existing design on your desktop. Try saying: "Generate a dark mode version of this illustration."

Press and hold the Fn key anywhere on macOS to launch it, or click the new screen sharing button at the end of the "Ask Gemini" prompt box. Gemini will display a floating capsule-shaped button containing a sound wave pattern at the bottom of the screen.

Please ensure you have updated the macOS version of Gemini to the latest version (1.88). This new voice feature is rolling out globally to all users, currently supporting English, with more languages "coming soon."
